description: CDK "Price Breaks by Source" parts pricing matrix exports, one folder per store. Newest dated file is current; older files are kept as history.

notes: Source description export also on file (optional input).
Matrix labor type confirmed 2026-11-05 (Prescott peer comparison, Aug-Oct 2026 labor-type profile).
Customer-pay price field is PRICE10 (other Toyota stores use PRICE6).
Source 200 has only a LIST-field rule (no PRICE10 rule) - untested.
Matrix labor type confirmed 2026-11-05 (Prescott peer comparison, Aug-Oct 2026 labor-type profile).
Sources 140-145 set the price to another stored price field (PRICE7), which Qlik does not carry - untested.
Matrix labor type confirmed 2026-11-05 (Prescott peer comparison, Aug-Oct 2026 labor-type profile).
Also carries LIST-field rules (how list is filled, e.g. $0 list -> cost +67%); not customer-pay pricing.
Matrix change went live 2026-02-02 on GM parts sources 120/123/999 (found in the Nov 2026 audit).
One cost-based rule on every priced source (100-104, 106, 145, 995); 996-999 = list. Source 160 has a LIST-field rule only; source 200 has no rule.
Matrix change went live the week of 2026-07-27 (step change in current-matrix match rate).
CCCE = Hyundai Complimentary Care (factory-paid maintenance), not matrix-priced. CEX = extended warranty.
Brake pads sell at a flat $140.95 (not matrix) before and after the change.
Matrix labor types confirmed 2026-11-09: CS, CSQ (quick lane), CTPMS. CSSC/CEXT reimbursed, CACC unclear, CSEMP employee, CPPM prepaid at cost.

Source 200 = Subaru dealer parts, LIST + 300% down to LIST + 20% by list band. 202/300/400 = list. 301 tires = cost + 32% (list up to $599.99). 999 windshields = cost + 450% (looks like a setup error).
Source 203 prices at its own stored PRICE6 (not in Qlik) - untestable. Source 201 has a LIST-field rule only.
Store splits visits onto 'C' suffix ROs (mostly the customer-pay work on a warranty visit).
